collection.description: A teenager thinks the chief is annoying and asks why anyone should listen to them.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (teen) thinks the {@chief} is annoying and asks why anyone should listen to them.

choices.label: Ask the {@Chief} to Explain a Decision

a1.name: Outcome A1
a1.text: The {@chief} provides a reason (teen) had not heard.

a2.name: Outcome A2
a2.text: The explanation remains unconvincing, and (teen) respectfully asks how decisions can be reviewed.

b1.name: Outcome B1
b1.text: They distinguish rules that protect people from rules based on convenience.

b2.name: Outcome B2
b2.text: The teens disagree sharply but agree that mockery is not a substitute for an argument.

c1.name: Outcome C1
c1.text: The {@chief} accepts a small change after seeing (teen)'s plan.

c2.name: Outcome C2
c2.text: The {@chief} declines and explains what evidence would justify reconsideration.

d1.name: Outcome D1
d1.text: (elder) recalls a beloved {@chief} who made a serious mistake.

d2.name: Outcome D2
d2.text: (elder) tells of an unpopular {@chief} whose tedious caution once prevented harm.
